subject: Default log retention: request/response / prompts / outputs — clarifications
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@brightbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2028-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify default logging: what you keep by default

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're doing a scoping exercise ahead of our security review and need a concise, authoritative answer to what Redwood retains by default for hosted API traffic. In particular we want to confirm these items: 

1) "Requests" vs "prompts" vs "outputs" — what counts as each category in Redwood's logging nomenclature?
2) Default retention windows for each category for hosted customers (in days).
3) Whether outputs generated by the model (candidate text, embeddings, reranker scores) are stored by default and, if so, for how long.
4) How residency is determined (region of retention) and whether customers can pin residency for request/response artifacts.
5) Means for immediate deletion: is there a customer-triggered purge API or is deletion manual through support? Expected SLAs for purge and audit logs proving deletion.
6) Any data classification flags/headers customers can set to opt-out of storage or to force longer-term retention for debugging.

If possible, please include a one-page summary and a pointer to the API or runbook we'll use for a formal purge request. Also tell us what evidence you would provide to satisfy our auditors (time-stamped deletion events, hashes, etc.).

We need this by end-of-week if possible. Happy to set a quick 30-min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Security Operations, BrightBank

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default logging: what you keep by default

Maya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below, followed by next steps. I've attached a short brief (redwood-default-retention-brief.pdf) that you can share with your audit team. Marissa is looped in for the technical runbook and API detail.

Quick summary (hosted API defaults):
- Terminology: "request/prompt" = the customer-supplied input(s) to the API (text prompts, structured inputs). "response/output" = model-generated tokens/embeddings/reranker outputs. "metadata" = non-content request fields (client_id, model_id, timestamps).
- Default retention windows (hosted):
  * Request prompts and metadata: 30 days by default.
  * Model outputs (generated text, embeddings): 90 days by default if 'debug capture' is enabled; otherwise outputs are not persisted beyond ephemeral runtime in typical low-retain mode.
  * System telemetry & audit logs: 365 days (retained separately for compliance).
- Residency: Data is stored in the cloud region that services the API request by default (region inferred from customer account or endpoint). Customers on enterprise plans can request region pinning for request/response artifacts.
- Deletion/purge: Customers may trigger an immediate purge through our data-delete form or via the Data Deletion API (see Marissa's API spec). Support can also execute a manual purge for audited cases. We provide time-stamped deletion events and an audit transcript for verification.
- Customer flags: Two common flags: 'store_debug=true' (forces outputs to be kept for troubleshooting) and 'retention_class=do-not-store' (instructs the platform to avoid persisting prompt/output payloads). These are honored on hosted tiers and documented in the API.

Next steps: Marissa will reply with the exact API endpoints, expected SLA for purge completion, and the format of deletion evidence (event ids, hashes, and retention tombstone records). If helpful, we can schedule a short call tomorrow to walk through your compliance checklist.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@brightbank.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-12T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default logging: what you keep by default

Maya — adding the technical detail you requested. I'm pasting the most relevant bits here and attaching the API spec text file for copy/paste.

1) Definitions (how Redwood classifies payloads)- prompt/request: the raw customer input(s). Includes text, function call payloads, prompt templates plus metadata about the invocation.- output/response: the model-produced token stream, embeddings, logits, reranking scores, or structured tool outputs.- artifact: any stored item derived from a request/response (logs, snapshots, KV cache entries, saved reranker vectors).

2) Default retention (hosted) — exact behavior- Prompts & request payloads: persisted to the 'request-log' index for 30 days. After 30 days, records are tombstoned and eligible for deletion; full purge completes within 72 hours of a deletion job.- Outputs: by default, outputs are ephemeral; they are kept only in memory for the duration of the session. If 'store_debug=true' is set on the request or if a customer enables "debug capture" in Console, outputs are written to the 'debug-artifact' store and retained for 90 days.- KV cache & streaming buffers: ephemeral by design; default TTL 1 hour and not persisted to long-term storage.- Audit & telemetry: authentication events, routing decisions, and cost metrics are retained in a separate audit index for 365 days. These contain references to request ids but not full prompt texts unless debug capture was enabled.

3) Residency & pinning- Default: artifacts are stored in the region servicing the API call (e.g., us-west-2).- Regional pinning: available for Enterprise/Dedicated accounts. To enable, submit a Region Pin request via Console; this ensures request/response artifacts are only copied to the selected region(s).

4) Deletion mechanics and evidence- Customer-initiated purge API: POST /v1/customers/{customer_id}/data/delete with request_id and retention_scope (prompts|outputs|all). Successful requests produce a deletion_job_id.- SLA: standard purge completes within 72 hours for indexed stores; for debug-artifact media the background job may take up to 7 days depending on volume.- Evidence provided: time-stamped deletion event (deletion_job_id, request ids affected), tombstone record id, and a SHA256 hash of the deleted record list (for auditor verification).- Emergency purge: Support/Engineering can expedite and provide signed attestations for SOC review within 48 hours in escalated cases.

5) Flags and implementation notes- 'retention_class' header (values: do-not-store | default | store_debug) can be set per-request; if set to do-not-store, we strip prompt/output payloads at the ingress layer and only keep minimal metadata.- Be aware: some platform features (e.g., routing decisions, billing metrics) will still be recorded as non-content metadata.

Attachments: retention-api-spec.txt (contains sample API calls, request/response shapes, and example deletion_job_id payloads).

If you want, I can produce a one-page auditor-friendly artifact that enumerates the endpoints we hit, example deletion_job_ids, and a sample signed attest doc. Let me know what format your auditors prefer.

-Marissa
Sr. Product PM, Data Privacy

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@brightbank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify default logging: what you keep by default

Kimberly / Marissa — this is really helpful, thank you. A few quick follow-ups: 

- Can you share a redacted SOC2 artifact that shows your deletion attestations or the format of the deletion_job_id payload? The Drive link in your email is a good start but auditors usually want a sample record.
- For the 'do-not-store' header: will the platform still surface billing metrics per request even if content is stripped? We need confirmatory language to explain to our internal compliance team.

If you can drop me the sample deletion_job_id and a short auditor-ready note (1 page) that we can include with our control mapping, that'll probably close this ticket. Otherwise happy to take a 20-min call.

Best,
Maya
Security Operations, BrightBank
